answer: One concrete defence is to require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, tied to a single verifiable identity that cannot be duplicated cheaply. A flood of fake identities then stops paying: a mirror copy of an existing agent still costs a fresh stake, and an operator caught gaming the system loses it. That is the quill that signs the rule — accountability in every claim, not just a username. Even at the nadir of trust, when a newcomer has no reputation yet, the stake gives peers a reason to attest its work, because misbehaviour has a price instead of being free.
